name: Acetaminophen (Paracetamol)
description: First-line analgesic and antipyretic medication indicated for mild-to-moderate pain and fever reduction.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 500 mg to 1,000 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose must not exceed 4,000 mg in 24 hours to prevent hepatotoxicity.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Rare at therapeutic doses. Nausea, rash, or allergic reactions. Acute hepatic failure may occur with overdose.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Avoid concurrent alcohol intake. Never combine with other multi-symptom OTC medicines containing acetaminophen.

name: Ibuprofen
description: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug used for relief of acute pain, swelling, fever, and musculoskeletal inflammation.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 200 mg to 400 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours with food. Do not exceed 1,200 mg daily for OTC use without physician supervision.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Dyspepsia, heartburn, stomach pain, dizziness, fluid retention.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Contraindicated in active peptic ulcer disease or third trimester of pregnancy. Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants.

name: Amoxicillin
description: Broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotic indicated for respiratory tract, ear, nose, and bacterial urinary infections.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 250 mg to 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours depending on infection severity. Complete full prescribed regimen.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, erythematous maculopapular rash.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Contraindicated in severe penicillin allergy (risk of anaphylaxis). May reduce oral contraceptive efficacy.

name: Loratadine
description: Non-sedating selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist for seasonal allergic rhinitis, sneezing, and urticaria.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults and children 6 years and older: 10 mg orally once daily. Do not exceed 10 mg in 24 hours.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Headache, dry mouth, drowsiness (rare at therapeutic doses), fatigue.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Dose adjustment required in severe renal or hepatic impairment. Avoid combination with sedative antihistamines.

name: Omeprazole
description: Suppresses gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+-ATPase proton pump for GERD and peptic ulcers.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 20 mg to 40 mg once daily, taken 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Swallow capsule whole without chewing.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Headache, abdominal pain, flatulence, nausea, diarrhea or constipation.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Prolonged therapy may reduce hypomagnesemia and vitamin B12 absorption. May interact with clopidogrel and methotrexate.

name: Naproxen
description: Long-acting nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic indicated for arthritis, musculoskeletal pain, and dysmenorrhea.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 220 mg to 500 mg orally twice daily with meals or a full glass of water. Maximum 1,500 mg/day under medical supervision.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Stomach upset, heartburn, nausea, constipation, dizziness, peripheral edema.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Black box warning for cardiovascular thrombotic events and gastrointestinal ulceration/bleeding.

name: Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid)
description: Irreversible cyclooxygenase inhibitor used for cardiovascular prophylaxis (low-dose) and mild pain/inflammation relief.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Cardioprotection: 81 mg to 100 mg orally once daily. Acute analgesic dose: 325 mg to 650 mg every 4 hours as needed.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Gastric irritation, occult bleeding, tinnitus at elevated doses, bruising.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Never administer to children or adolescents recovering from viral illness due to risk of Reye syndrome.

name: Azithromycin
description: Broad-spectrum macrolide antibiotic indicated for community-acquired pneumonia, strep pharyngitis, and skin infections.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 500 mg single dose on day 1, followed by 250 mg once daily on days 2 through 5 (Z-Pak regimen).

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Gastrointestinal cramping, diarrhea, nausea, transient transaminase elevations.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Use caution in patients with baseline prolonged QT interval or proarrhythmic cardiac conditions.

name: Ciprofloxacin
description: Potent bactericidal fluoroquinolone targeting bacterial DNA gyrase; indicated for complicated UTI and bone infections.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 250 mg to 750 mg orally every 12 hours depending on infection site and microbiological severity.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Nausea, diarrhea, headache, photosensitivity, restlessness.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Black box warning for tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and CNS toxicities. Avoid dairy/antacids during dosing.

name: Doxycycline
description: Broad-spectrum tetracycline antibiotic indicated for atypical pneumonia, Lyme disease, acne vulgaris, and rickettsial diseases.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 100 mg orally every 12 hours on day 1, followed by 100 mg once or twice daily. Take with full glass of water sitting upright.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Esophageal irritation, nausea, cutaneous photosensitivity, tooth discoloration in pediatrics.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Contraindicated in pregnancy and children under 8 years. Chelation occurs with iron, calcium, and antacids.

name: Lisinopril
description: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor indicated for essential hypertension, congestive heart failure, and post-MI recovery.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: Initial 10 mg orally once daily; titrated up to 20 mg to 40 mg daily based on target blood pressure.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Dry persistent cough, dizziness, hypotension, hyperkalemia, elevated creatinine.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Black box warning for fetal toxicity in pregnancy. Monitor serum potassium and renal panel periodically.

name: Amlodipine
description: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker promoting peripheral vascular vasodilation for hypertension and chronic stable angina.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 5 mg orally once daily; maximum dose 10 mg once daily. May be taken with or without food.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Peripheral edema (ankle swelling), flushing, dizziness, palpitations, fatigue.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Use caution in severe aortic stenosis or severe hepatic impairment. Limit simvastatin dosage when co-administered.

name: Atorvastatin
description: Statin lipid-lowering agent indicated for primary hypercholesterolemia and secondary prevention of cardiovascular atherosclerotic events.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 10 mg to 80 mg orally once daily, taken at any time of day with or without food.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Myalgia, arthralgia, diarrhea, nasopharyngitis, dyspepsia.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Contraindicated in active liver disease and pregnancy. Report unexplained muscle tenderness or dark tea-colored urine promptly.

name: Metoprolol
description: Cardioselective beta-adrenergic blocker indicated for hypertension, angina pectoris, hemodynamically stable heart failure, and post-MI.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Metoprolol Tartrate: 25 mg to 100 mg twice daily. Metoprolol Succinate ER: 25 mg to 200 mg once daily with or immediately after a meal.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Bradycardia, fatigue, dizziness, hypotension, cold extremities, bronchospasm.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Do not abruptly discontinue; taper over 1 to 2 weeks to prevent rebound angina or myocardial infarction.

name: Metformin
description: First-line oral antidiabetic biguanide that decreases hepatic glucose production and enhances peripheral insulin sensitivity.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: Initial 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily with meals; titrated to maximum 2,000 mg to 2,550 mg daily.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating, metallic taste, vitamin B12 depletion.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Black box warning for lactic acidosis. Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²).

name: Pantoprazole
description: Substituted benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor indicated for healing of erosive esophagitis and pathological hypersecretory states.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: 40 mg orally once daily for up to 8 weeks. Take approximately 30 minutes before breakfast.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, abdominal discomfort, flatulence.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Long-term usage associated with Clostridioides difficile diarrhea, hypomagnesemia, and bone fracture risk.

name: Cetirizine
description: Potent peripheral H1 receptor antagonist for symptomatic management of allergic rhinitis, perennial allergies, and chronic urticaria.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults and adolescents 12+: 5 mg to 10 mg orally once daily depending on symptom severity.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Somnolence, fatigue, dry mouth, pharyngitis, dizziness.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Avoid concurrent alcohol or CNS depressants. Dose adjustment indicated in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.

name: Albuterol (Salbutamol)
description: Short-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist (SABA) providing rapid relief of acute bronchospasm and exercise-induced asthma.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Inhalation aerosol: 1 to 2 inhalations (90 mcg/actuation) every 4 to 6 hours as needed for acute wheezing. For exercise prophylaxis: 2 puffs 15 minutes before exertion.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Tremor, nervousness, tachycardia, palpitations, headache, throat irritation.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Beta-blockers can antagonize bronchodilatory effect and provoke severe bronchospasm in asthmatic individuals.

name: Sertraline
description: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) indicated for major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and PTSD.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: Initial 50 mg orally once daily in the morning or evening; titrated up to maximum 200 mg daily at weekly intervals.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Nausea, insomnia, diarrhea, dizziness, dry mouth, sexual dysfunction, tremor.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Black box warning for suicidal thoughts in young adults. Contraindicated with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs).

name: Escitalopram
description: Highly selective pure serotonin reuptake inhibitor indicated for acute and maintenance treatment of generalized anxiety disorder and major depression.

details.title: Typical Dosage
details.content: Adults: Initial 10 mg orally once daily; can be increased to 20 mg daily after a minimum of one week of therapy.

details.title: Common Side Effects
details.content: Insomnia, somnolence, increased sweating, nausea, fatigue, decreased libido.

details.title: Interactions & Warnings
details.content: Contraindicated with MAOIs or pimozide. Risk of serotonin syndrome when combined with triptans or tramadol.
